title: Amounts Hosts Owe Roamhaven: Deduction and Recovery Across Payout Methods
content:
An amount a host owes Roamhaven is deducted from a Payout Methods balance. The amounts owed are four: the host-funded share of a guest refund issued after the payout release (the refunded amount less the host service fee refunded on it), a host cancellation penalty, a protection premium, and a guest damage payment later reversed.

## Where the deduction is taken

- An amount tied to a stay is deducted from the undisbursed balance of the method the stay's earnings were released to.
- An amount not tied to a stay is deducted from the undisbursed balance of the default method.

## When the balance cannot cover it

Where that balance cannot cover the amount, the remainder is recovered from the next released earnings on **any** of the host's payout methods, oldest deficit first. The host's deficit at any moment is the sum of the deductions not yet covered by later inflows, that is, the negative part of the undisbursed balances across all the host's payout methods.

## Once per source record

A deduction is applied once per source record. Each deduction names the record that created the amount owed (the refund, penalty, premium or reversal); where the payout ledger already shows a deduction of that kind naming that record, no second deduction is applied for it.

## Deficits that remain unrecovered

A deficit still unrecovered 90 calendar days after it arose leaves support for Roamhaven collections; support does not settle it, write it off or take a card payment for it.

## Hypothetical worked case

An imagined host owes a USD 300.00 cancellation penalty tied to a stay whose earnings were released to a PayPal method holding USD 120.00. The deduction is taken from that PayPal balance, which cannot cover it: USD 180.00 remains as a deficit. The next earnings released, say USD 500.00 to the host's Direct Deposit (ACH) method a week later, recover that USD 180.00 first, being the oldest deficit. Had the deficit stayed unrecovered for 90 calendar days after it arose, it would have left support for collections.

## Points of judgement

| Question | Answer from these terms |
|---|---|
| Is a refund clawback the full refunded amount? | No: it is the refunded amount less the host service fee refunded on it. |
| Can the same penalty be deducted twice because it was entered twice? | No: one deduction per source record. |
| May support take a card payment for a deficit that has passed 90 days? | No: it has left support for Roamhaven collections. |
